newsitem.title: USA: Wheat, corn, milk sales down $6 bln in 1997 - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Wheat, corn, milk sales down $6 bln in 1997 - USDA.

text.p: Lower wheat, corn and milk prices will reduce cash receipts for those commodities by $6 billion this year, Agriculture Department chief economist Keith Collins said Tuesday.
During a Senate hearing on price volatility, Collins said the new "freedom to farm" law "has not increased dramatically" the degree of volatility in grain and livestock prices.

Using a standard statistical measurement, the coefficient of variation, Collins said wheat prices were less than one-half as volatile as they were during the 1970s, but about 25 percent more than the 1980s.
Volatility in corn prices was less than the 1970s and 1980s, and soybean prices also were less variable in the 1990s than in the two preceding decades.
Livestock prices were about as variable as during the 1980s, he said. Milk prices this decade have been 50 percent more volatile than during the 1980s but still far less than the 1970s.
Collins also told the Senate Agriculture Committee that exports "are contributing to less of the variation in grain and oilseed prices than earlier decades."
